content:
maria: Heads up — CI deploys to the gpu-pool started failing around 10:02 UTC. Several pods stuck Pending with scheduler events saying SA denied access.
kevin: Any logs from the scheduler or kube-apiserver audit?
jen-sre: I pulled the pod events and kubelet logs on the node. Here's the most relevant event: 

```
Normal  FailedScheduling  2m (x3 over 5m)  default-scheduler  0/10 nodes are available: 10 
message: 'pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims, pods with storageclass gpufast require kms:Decrypt'
```

kevin: Wait — "require kms:Decrypt"? We don't decrypt anything in k8s scheduler. Where's that coming from?
alex-sec: That's from the init container that fetches encrypted model shards from the object store via our kms wrapper. The CI job mounts a PVC that triggers the init container which calls KMS to unwrap a per-volume key.
maria: Right. The failing SA is `ci-gpu-scheduler-sa` used by the CI deploy Job controller when scheduling onto dedicated GPU nodes. Audit log shows KMS permission denied: 

```
{"verb":"decrypt","user":"system:serviceaccount:ci:ci-gpu-scheduler-sa","resource":"cryptoKeys","status":"Denied","reason":"permissionDenied"}
```

jen-sre: I also checked rolebindings — `ci-gpu-scheduler-sa` is bound to `ci-deployer` ClusterRole which we recently stripped of broad cloudkms permissions in the last least-privilege refactor. Looks like we missed adding kms:Decrypt for the init flow.
kevin: Is it safe to just add kms:decrypt to that ClusterRole? I worry about widening privileges for CI jobs.
alex-sec: Prefer creating a minimal role specifically for the init workflow: a KMS role scoped to the single key resource ARN and a Kubernetes RoleBinding that only gives the SA that ScopedCloudKMS access. We should avoid cluster-wide KMS permissions.
ops-bot: deploy-bot triggered CI retry for build #2456 — re-run in progress (:arrows_counterclockwise:).
maria: Proposed quick fix for hot path: temporarily add a short-lived ClusterRoleBinding to unblock CI, expiration 2 hours, tracked in incident board. Then follow up with scoped KMS key policy + a dedicated SA for the init job. Thoughts?
jen-sre: +1 for temporary unblock but log it and rotate. Also add audit webhook to filter for kms decrypt denies so we can surface regressions.
kevin: I'll prep the ClusterRoleBinding snippet. Example: 

```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: ci-gpu-kms-temporary-unblock
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: ci-gpu-scheduler-sa
  namespace: ci
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: ci-deployer
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

kevin: ETA 10m to apply with an expiry note in the description. Then we should add an IAM/KMS policy: allow kms:Decrypt for resource `projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/gpu/cryptoKeys/gpu-volume-key` for principal `serviceAccount:ci:ci-init-sa` only.
alex-sec: I'll draft the KMS policy and the least-priv role. Also want a short-term compensating control: alert on any ClusterRoleBinding creations for deploy roles so we catch accidental broadening.
maria: After unblock, action items: 1) create scoped SA `ci-init-sa` and update job to use it (alex), 2) create KMS key policy allowing only that SA (alex), 3) remove temporary ClusterRoleBinding and rotate relevant keys (kevin), 4) add audit alert for kms permissionDenied events (jen-sre).
jen-sre: I'll add the audit alert rule. Suggest we tag the incident and include the temp CRB name so it's easy to track.
kevin: Applied temp CRB and retriggered CI. ops-bot shows build now pending scheduling — looks like pods are moving to Running.
maria: CI passed on retry — good. Leaving this thread for postmortem notes.
alex-sec: I'll post PRs for the scoped SA + KMS policy and a small doc on "GPU init least-privilege pattern".
jen-sre: Recommend we also add an integration test in CI that validates the init SA can kms:Decrypt but generic deploy SA cannot. Catch regressions early.
maria: Agree. Thanks everyone. Marking incident as "resolved - temporary fix applied, follow-up work tracked" :white_check_mark:
